title: The Mother Lode
logline: Virginia Mosby and Loretta Stinson meet by accident at brunch and become instant best friends, two breezy mothers who overshare without noticing, and they start swapping stories about their sons. Ted and Barney team up to break up the friendship, every sabotage brings the moms closer, and Robin, Marshall and Lily enjoy the leaks far too much until they find out what the moms know about them.
coldOpen: Kids, every man has one person who knows every humiliating thing he's ever done: his mother. In the spring of 2012, Uncle Barney and I found out there's something worse. Two mothers.

couch.line: Wait. Grandma and Loretta? They do everything together.
They do now, Penny. This is the story of how that happened. And how hard I fought it.

guests.name: Marguerite Fontaine
guests.role: A retired dinner-theater actress Barney hires to steal his mother away from Virginia. Never breaks character, curtsies after every line, and turns out to overshare about her own son even more than the moms do

scenes.summary: Ted brings Virginia to Castellano's because nobody he knows would ever go there; Barney brought Loretta for the same reason. The moms meet and become best friends in under a minute, then swap the floor-plan proposal and the clip-on tie. Barney cites the Bro Code. The moms declare girls' week and leave the boys the check. Button: Barney has broken up plenty of friendships, mostly his own.

beats.line: Every spring, your grandmother came to New York to see one show and tell me one thing I'd spend a year forgetting.
Teddy, I have news. I'm modeling for a life drawing class at the community center.
Like a still life? With a bowl of fruit?
Honey. I am the bowl of fruit.
Mom, I picked Castellano's because nobody I know would ever set foot in here. Let's keep it that way.
Barnabus, your father sent a postcard. He's a jazz trumpeter now. In Reno.
Mom, last year he was a ventriloquist.
Your father has range, sweetie.
Barney?
Ted? What are you doing here? Nobody I know would ever set foot in here.
It's also the last restaurant in Manhattan where I haven't slept with the hostess.
Barnabus, is that the Ted? The one who says actually?
Actually.
Fair.
Loretta Stinson. Do you also tell your son things he's begging you not to?
Every Sunday! It's my favorite part of the phone call. He makes a little noise, like a kettle.
Barnabus does the kettle too! Where have you been all my life?
Ohio, mostly.
Ted, code red. Bro Code, Article sixty-six. A Bro's mother shall never come within fifty feet of another Bro's mother.
Why fifty feet?
That's the range of a mother's whisper.
Loretta, when Teddy was six, he proposed to the girl next door. With a floor plan.
Did she say yes?
She asked for more closet space.
It was a starter home!
Oh, I love him. Barnabus slept in a clip-on tie until he was twelve.
Like a tiny banker!
It was for posture!
Mom!
Listen to them. Two little kettles.
Ginny, I'm in town all week.
So am I! Girls' week!
Boys, get the check. Ginny and I have forty years of catching up to do. On you.
Barney, we have to break them up. But I've never broken up a friendship before.
I have. Mostly mine.

scenes.summary: The moms have added Lily to their group chat, and Robin, Marshall and Lily are feasting on leaks: the parking garage, the Easter Bunny, Professor Hootington. Marshall is hurt Ted never told him about the owl. Barney pitches divide and conquer; his imagined catfight cutaway. The others doubt it. Button: two new leaks, Ted and Barney yell 'Mom!' at Lily.

beats.line: Ted cried at a parking garage, and Barney is scared of the Easter Bunny. This is the best day of my life.
beats.title: Ginny and Lolo

messages.text: Teddy cried at the ribbon cutting for a parking garage. Happy tears.
Barnabus was scared of the Easter Bunny until he was nineteen. Still crosses the street.

beats.line: I've started a binder on Barney. It has tabs. One tab is just the Easter Bunny.
Lily, why is my mother texting you?
They added me to their group chat at nine a.m. Ginny says I'm the cool one.
I've already been to brunch, a pedicure and a second brunch.
It's Monday. You teach kindergarten.
I told the kids it was nap day. All day.
Ted. A parking garage?
It had a cantilevered ramp, Marshall. Anyone would have cried.
No one would have cried.
The Easter Bunny, Barney?
It was six feet tall and it never blinked. That's not a bunny. That's a predator.
Oh, and Ginny sent a photo of Professor Hootington.
Who is Professor Hootington?
He was a stuffed owl. He had tenure.
Fourteen years, Ted. Fourteen years, and you never told me about the owl.
I was going to tell you!
When? On my deathbed? Marshall, before you go, there's an owl?
Enough. Ted and I are breaking those two up.
Break them up? They're like two Lilys who've been to Atlantic City.
I'm terrified of them, and I want them to adopt me.
It's simple. Divide and conquer. I tell my mom that Ginny called her tacky.
And I tell my mom that Loretta called her a gossip.
Two moms, two insults, zero brunches.
Loretta. I hear you called me a gossip.
And I hear you called me tacky. In this blouse?
That blouse looks like a disco ball went to a funeral.
Divide and conquer, Ted. Julius Caesar invented it. I suited it up.
That's not how moms work.
You tell a mom she's a gossip, she doesn't get mad. She gets material.
Trust us. By Thursday, those two will be strangers.
Ooh, new ones. Ted had a rat tail until tenth grade. And Barney lost a baby pageant to a girl named Bridget.
Mom!
You both just yelled Mom at Lily.

scenes.summary: Montage: every sabotage brings the moms closer (the gossip lie, two hours on the wrong train, a hired rival who defects). At Barney's, Ted and Barney despair. Robin, Marshall and Lily storm in: the moms are swapping stories about them too, from Ted and Barney. The trio switches sides. The nuclear option: tell each mom the other insulted her son, then put them in one cab with Barney driving. Button: Lily already told the doorman.

beats.line: Kids, over the next three days, Uncle Barney and I tried everything.
Teddy says you called me a gossip!
Ginny, we are gossips! Isn't it wonderful?
Two hours on the wrong train, Lolo.
And we still haven't run out of stories about the boys!
Ladies, I'm Marguerite. Forget each other. I am your new best friend.
Barnabus is paying you, isn't he? Sit down and tell us about your son.
Marguerite quit on Thursday, refunded Barney's money and joined their book club.
Ted, I once ended a six-year engagement with one well-placed earring. I can't break up two women who met on Sunday.
Every time we try, they get closer. We're not breaking them up. We're setting them up.
Oh, God. Ted. We're the Lily of this situation.
I heard that. And I'm letting it go, because I'm here to help.
Ted. Why does your mother know I bit a mall Santa?
In fairness, it was a very slow Thanksgiving.
Your mother asked me to sing at her birthday. She requested the one about the mall.
She's a big fan.
Of what? I've never sung a note in my life. Or been to a mall.
And Ginny told Loretta I cried at the end of a Bigfoot documentary.
Baby, you did.
Because they didn't find him, Lily!
So you're in. Good. Because there's one thing no mother ever forgives.
An insult to her son. Robin tells my mom that Ginny called me shallow.
And Lily tells my mom that Loretta called me pretentious.
So, the truth.
I can't lie to Ginny. She has those big Mosby eyes. Like a deer that just heard about load-bearing walls.
Lilypad, you can't lie to anyone. You told the cable guy about my birthday surprise.
He asked how my day was!
So you tell them at six. At six-oh-five, they're trapped together in one cab. And I'm driving.
You can drive a cab?
I've had a hack license since 2006.
Why?
Please.
Forty minutes on the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway at rush hour. No friendship survives that.
Fine. But I'm warning you. I crack.
Lily, it's one day. You'll be fine.
I already told your doorman. He says good luck.

scenes.summary: Barney drives in a hoodie and a mustache as Gustav, Ted rides shotgun in a cap. The bait worked: the moms are frosty, and Lily and Robin embellished. Each mom defends her son, and the defenses are the heart: the mother-in-law suite in the six-year-old's floor plan, the clip-on tie that made him the man of the house. Ted and Barney whisper 'Mom' and blow their cover. Barney's fish sticks undercut. Lily's confession text arrives too late. The moms are touched: their sons are best friends, just like them. They exit; the father runner pays off. Future Ted: the floor plan, and your mother asked for more closet space.

beats.line: Ted, I'm wearing a hoodie. If I die tonight, bury me in a suit. And tell no one.
Relax. In that mustache, nobody will ever recognize you.
That's what scares me.
Loretta.
Virginia.
It's working.
Good evening, ladies. I am Gustav, a normal cab driver. Where to?
MacLaren's pub. And quickly, Gustav. I'd like to be out of this cab.
Of course. I know a shortcut. It is forty minutes.
Lily told me what you said about Teddy. That he's a pretentious loser who'll die alone.
And Robin told me you called Barnabus a shallow man-child in a rented tuxedo.
Rented? Robin went off script.
Lily added the dying alone.
That part's just good research.
Let me tell you something about my son. That floor plan he drew when he was six?
It had a room in it for me. A mother-in-law suite. He was six, and he was worried I'd be lonely.
I've kept every drawing he ever made me. Two hundred and twelve. He thinks I don't listen.
Well, Barnabus is not shallow. And his father wasn't a trumpeter. Or a ventriloquist.
He was just gone. So every night I worked, my nine-year-old made dinner. In a clip-on tie.
He said if he dressed like the man of the house, I wouldn't notice there wasn't one.
Mom.
Teddy?
Barnabus?
The fish sticks were blackened on purpose. It's a Cajun technique.
Ginny. Did you really call Barnabus shallow?
Never! I said he owns a lot of suits. Did you call Teddy a loser?
Of course not. I called him a romantic. It's the same thing, in a nicer sweater.
Oh, Lily cracked. Eleven minutes. That's a personal best.
beats.title: Lily

messages.text: Ginny, I'm so sorry. It's a setup. Nobody insulted anybody.
The cab driver is Barney. Ted is in the front seat. In a hat.

beats.line: Ginny, look at them. Two grown men in disguise, working together, to hide from their mothers.
They tell each other everything, don't they?
Ginny. They're us.
Pull over, Gustav. We'll walk from here. Teddy, call me Sunday. I'll have news.
And sit up straight, Barnabus. You're driving just like your father.
Which one?
All of them, sweetie.
So. A clip-on tie.
A mother-in-law suite. At six.
Bro Code, Article sixty-seven. What a Bro hears in a cab stays in the cab.
You just made that up.
They're all made up, Ted. That's what makes them binding.
Kids, Uncle Barney and I never did break them up. Grandma and Loretta have been best friends ever since.
So did Grandma ever show Mom the floor plan?
The first night I brought her home. Your mother studied it for a long time. Then she asked for more closet space.
